title: Preserve ordinary fitting when metadata routing is disabled
answers: Why can Pipeline fit with its default transform_input when routing is disabled?
Why does transform_input=["X_val"] raise but the default tuple does not?
Why does passing X_val to fit fail without metadata routing?
body:
Invariant: With metadata routing disabled, the default transform_input=("X_val",) must allow ordinary fitting without validation metadata.
Enforcement: sklearn/pipeline.py:Pipeline.fit rejects transform_input only when it is truthy and differs from ("X_val",); None and empty lists or tuples also bypass this guard.
Boundary: The exemption compares the actual value, so ["X_val"] still triggers the transform_input guard. Passing X_val to fit with the default instead produces the usual "Pipeline.fit does not accept" error.
Regression coverage: sklearn/tests/test_pipeline.py:test_transform_input_no_slep6 checks custom-input rejection, ordinary default fitting, and rejection of supplied X_val; removing the default exemption would break ordinary fitting with routing disabled.
applies: Pipeline.fit compatibility and error handling when metadata routing is disabled.
